text: A T1 carries 24 DS0 channels; an E1 carries 30 plus signalling. Why is a T1 1.544 Mb/s?
choices: 24 x 64 kb/s plus 8 kb/s of framing
It is an arbitrary standard rate
explanation: 24 x 64,000 = 1,536,000, plus one framing bit per 193-bit frame at 8,000 frames per second = 8,000 b/s, giving 1,544,000 b/s. The T1/E1 divergence is a genuine historical accident with real consequences for international circuits, and it persists in carrier price lists today.
